taskTitle: Monitor the key metrics associated with the workflow
content:
### Background:
- The management is very happy since the video can be viewed over the internet. 

- They have now requested you to setup a dashboard which will be used to monitor the resources involved in the workflow.

- You had a call with Ron regarding this and he suggested you to leverage CloudWatch metrics for the monitoring.

### Getting started:
- Your task is to setup a monitoring dashboard in CloudWatch service. 

- This dashboard will include relevant metrics associated to the services being used in your workflow. 

- The scripts are publicly available to help you create this dashboard. In this task, you will be using these scripts, which have been borrowed from the AWS Blog - **https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/media/cs-quick-and-easy-media-services-dashboards/**

- To use these scripts and deploy the dashboards, please follow the below steps:

1. **Log into the EC2 instance named `JAM-EC2-Instance`:**
>- Route to the EC2 console and click on **`Instances (Running)`**.
>- Out of the listed instances, select check-box on the **`JAM-EC2-Instance`** EC2 instance and click on the **`Connect`** button.
>- Out of the 4 shown options on the **`Connect to instance`** window, select **`Session Manager`** and click **`Connect`**.
>- This should open a new tab on your browser and log you into the EC2 instance.

2. **Download the scripts to deploy dashboard:**
>- Run command **`sudo su`** which will take you to the admin terminal.
>- Next, download the scripts and extract the content using command **`wget https://dlcc9uvp8v2in.cloudfront.net/LATEST.zip && unzip *.zip`**
>- Once downloaded exit the admin mode by using shortcut **`Ctrl+D`**
>- Go into the extracted folder containing the python scripts by running **`cd LATEST`**

3. **Deploy the MediaLive Dashboard:**
>- Run command **`sudo python3 MediaLive_dash_maker_v14.py`** to initiate the python script which will deplpoy the MediaLive Dashboard.
>- It will ask you to enter input as either of the 3 options **`[a]all channels, [t]tagged channels, or a [s]single channel`**: Enter **`s`**
>- It will further list all your MediaLive channels and ask you to select the MediaLive channels for which you want to deploy the dashboard.
>- Copy the MediaLive channel ID listed as **`ID`** (there will only be a single channel listed) and paste it as the input.
>- This will deploy the dashboard.

4. **Deploy the MediaPackage Dashboard:**
>- Run command **`sudo python3 MediaPackage_dashmaker_v07.py`** to initiate the python script which will deplpoy the MediaPackage Dashboard.
>- It will again ask you to enter input as either of the 3 options **`[a]all channels, [t]tagged channels, or a [s]single channel`**: Enter **`s`**
>- It will further list all your MediaPackage channels and ask you to enter the MediaPackage channel IDs for which you want to deploy the dashboard.
>- Copy the MediaPackage channel ID listed as **`CH-ID`** (there will only be a single channel listed) and paste it as the input.
>- This will deploy the dashboard.

5. **List the names of all deployed Dashboards:**
>- This is required as the input to our final command to create a combined dashboard.
>- Run **`ls | grep json`** to list all the dashboards created previously.

6. **Generate a combined dashboard**
>- Provide the JSON names listed in step 4 of all the dashboards that got deployed **as space separated inputs** to the command **`sudo python3 DashJoiner_v4.py`**
>- This will deploy your combined dashboard with a name format similar to **`Combined_dash_*******`**

### Services you will be using for this task:
- Amazon EC2

- Amazon CloudWatch

### Task validation:
- In order to validate this task, you need to enter the complete name of ANY ONE of the deployed metrics as seen on the combined dashboard named in format **`Combined_Dash_*******`**.

- The name of these metrics can be found on the top left corner of each metric box.

- Please enter the COMPLETE string as it is without truncating or redacting any part of it. ***NOTE: Please use any metric name except for the one that starts with **`ML:RTP Packet Status`*****
- Few examples:
>- **`ML:Metric name [stats used] - small description`** 
>- **`MP:Metric name - metric scope`**

- Once you enter any one of the correct metric names in the validation textbox and click on **`Submit Answer`** button, this task will be marked as completed!

challengeTitle: Live Streaming with AWS Media Services
content:
### Background:
- With our DASH stream working perfectly now and monitoring all set up, the management wants to provide a HLS playback URL as well to the viewers. This will be beneficial for devices that support HLS protocol. 

- On discussing with Ron, he was able to inform you that he had configuired 2 playback endpoints on MediaPackage, one for DASH and another for HLS.

- However, when testing playback via HLS, he was not able to get it to work before leaving for vacation.

- Your job now is to investigate why the HLS endpoint does not work, and rectify the issue. To test the playback, you can replace **`index.mpd`** with **`index.m3u8`**, so that your HLS playback URL should be of the form: **`https://cloudfront-domain-name/index.m3u8`**. 

### Getting started:
- Given that the DASH content is working fine, we can assume that the issue is not on MediaLive.

- Reason being, MediaLive pushes a single stream to MediaPackage, where the packaging to HLS and DASH actually occurs.

- Therefore, the next services in the data flow, after MediaLive, is MediaPackage.

- Investigate the settings associated with MediaPackage to figure out what is causing the HLS playback to fail, modify MediaPackage to rectify the issue, and save the changes.

- You can use this online player to test playback before and after fixing the issue: **`https://hlsjs.video-dev.org/demo/`**. Once you make changes in MediaPackage, please click on the **`Apply`** button within this online player.

### Services you will be using for this task:

- AWS Elemental MediaPackage

### Task validation:
- Once you fix the issue in MediaPackage, this task will automatically validate and will be marked as complete in a few moments!

- In order to immediately verify if your task is complete, you can check your progress by pressing the **`Check my progress`** button on the task details screen.

taskTitle: Pipeline Activator: Connect the S3 Trigger!
content:
## Background:
Your bank's loan processing system is deployed and ready, but there's a critical missing link - loan applications uploaded to S3 aren't triggering the automated processing pipeline. The Lambda functions exist and have proper permissions, but they're never invoked when PDF loan applications are uploaded to the bucket.

Amazon Simple Storage Service (S3) provides event notifications that can automatically trigger AWS Lambda functions when objects are created, modified, or deleted. In this challenge, you'll learn how to configure S3 event notifications to create a fully automated serverless processing pipeline for loan applications.

## Getting Started:
Sign in to the AWS Console through the Jam portal and go to the S3 service. You'll find a bucket with the prefix loan-processing-applications containing the storage for loan documents. A Lambda function named loan-processing-document-processor is ready to process uploaded PDFs. Your job is to connect these pieces together using S3 event notifications.

## Your Task:
Configure the S3 bucket to automatically trigger the Lambda function when PDF files are uploaded:
1. Configure S3 event notification for object creation events
2. Set up a filter to only trigger for `.pdf` files
3. Connect the notification to the `loan-processing-document-processor` Lambda function

## Inventory:

- An S3 bucket with the prefix: `loan-processing-applications`
- A Lambda function: `loan-processing-document-processor`
- Proper Lambda permissions already configured

## Services You Should Use:
- Amazon S3 Event Notifications
- AWS Lambda

## Task Validation:
The challenge completes automatically when the S3 event notification is properly configured. You can test your configuration by uploading a PDF document to the S3 bucket and verifying that the Lambda function is triggered.

taskTitle: Limit access to specific S3 prefixes
content:
### Background
The security consultant needs to access syslog files which are stored in a S3 bucket. Your company currently uses a single bucket to store all logs. You need to ensure that the consultant can only access objects within the syslog prefix. In addition to the prefix requirement, your company have specified that the consultant can only access the files during the month of April 2022 (`2022-04-01T00:00:00Z` -> `2022-04-30T23:59:59Z`).

### Your Task
Your colleague has already created an IAM policy (`SyslogS3AccessPolicy`), however it is too permissive. Your task is to update the policy to ensure the requirements are implemented, using least priviledge principles.

Bucket ARN: `arn:aws:s3:::company-security-logs`

1. Allow files in the `syslog` prefix to be listed
2. Allow files to be downloaded from the `syslog` prefix
3. Restrict access to the month of April 2022 only
4. Do not allow the user to list or access any files outside of the `syslog` prefix

#### Getting Started
Find the existing AWS IAM Policy `SyslogS3AccessPolicy` and edit the policy document to ensure the requirements above are provided for, whilst ensuring only least-privilege access is granted.

#### Inventory

### Background

The tool to scan the files has already been written in Python and deployed on the
AWS Lambda function *bucket-scan-function*. The Amazon Simple Storage Service (S3)
bucket used for the files to be scanned has a name that starts with *file-scanning-upload-*.
Unfortunately, it seems like something has been misconfigured as every time a file
to be scanned is uploaded, nothing happens. The team that did the deployment of the
tool swears that everything was working well until a new S3 bucket was created and
the previous one deleted.

Normally, the tool is supposed to be automatically triggered and it will output any
malware found in its log files. You have been tasked to fix this solution.

### Your Task
The development team has been using the [test_file.txt](https://aws-jam-challenge-resources.s3.amazonaws.com/malware-in-your-bucket/test_file.txt)
to test their tool. There's a special vulnerability in that file which when scanned 
provides a specific name. They've asked you to fix the scanning solution and asked you
to provide the name of that vulnerability once the scan is completed.

The upload of the file in the S3 bucket should automatically trigger the AWS Lambda 
function which will output the name of the vulnerability in its log files. Note that 
it may take 30 seconds after the upload for the Log Group to get created the first time.
If you don't see any log stream or received an error that there's no Log Group created, 
it means that you haven't completed the the challenge properly.

#### Background:
Galaxy Media Inc. has successfully launched their streaming service, but there's a critical security concern: anyone with the MediaPackage URLs can directly access their premium content, bypassing their CloudFront distribution. This poses a significant risk to their business model and content security.

#### Your Task:
Implement CDN Authorization to ensure that only requests coming through Galaxy Media's authorized CloudFront distribution can access content from MediaPackage, effectively preventing direct access to their valuable streaming content.

#### Inventory:
All required components are already configured in your AWS account:
- MediaPackage channel named 'MediaPackage_Channel' with HLS endpoint
- CloudFront distribution pointing to the MediaPackage endpoint
- IAM Role 'CDNAuthRole' with required permissions

The details of these resources can be found in the 'Output Properties' section above.

#### Services You Should Use:
- Amazon CloudFront - https://aws.amazon.com/cloudfront/
- AWS Elemental MediaPackage - https://aws.amazon.com/mediapackage/
- AWS Secrets Manager - https://aws.amazon.com/secrets-manager/

#### Getting Started:
1. Configure CloudFront:
   - Add a custom header named 'X-MediaPackage-CDNIdentifier'
   - Use a UUID v4 as the header value (you can generate one using any online third-party UUID generator)

2. Create a Secret:
   - Use AWS Secrets Manager to create a new secret
   - Key should be 'MediaPackageCDNIdentifier' and value should be same UUID v4
   - Make sure that the Secret Name is prefixed with 'MediaPackage/'

3. Enable CDN Authorization:
   - Modify the MediaPackage HLS endpoint and enable CDN authorization
   - Provide the requested information and save the changes.

You can refer to the MediaPackage documentation for more information: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/mediapackage/latest/ug/cdn-auth.html

#### Task Validation:
The task will automatically validate and be marked as complete once CDN Authorization is properly configured on MediaPackage endpoint and custom origin header added to the CloudFront distribution. You can check your progress at any time using the 'Check my progress' button on the task details screen.

2. Configure DRM on MediaPackage Endpoint:

   - Enable Package encryption
   - Configure package encryption:
     * Resource ID: Provide a unique identifier
     * System ID: As shared above
     * URL: Use the SPEKE API URL from output
     * IAM Role ARN: Use the SPEKE invoke role ARN from output

You can refer to the following documentation - https://docs.aws.amazon.com/mediapackage/latest/ug/using-encryption.html

#### Task Validation:
The task will be automatically validated once you have properly configured the DRM settings on the MediaPackage HLS endpoint.

challengeTitle: Midnight Mayhem: GitOps to the Rescue
content:
### **Background**
CloudNinja Corp's deployments are a disaster. Every manual deployment breaks something, customers complain, and the team works all night fixing problems. You're the GitOps hero brought in to end this chaos.

### **Your Mission**
Deploy and configure the core GitOps infrastructure components using Amazon Q Developer as your intelligent guide and EKS MCP Server as your Kubernetes specialist. 
You will establish your own Git repository server and Argo CD as your GitOps controller, creating the foundation for automated, Git-driven deployments that will 
eliminate human error and ensure consistent infrastructure state.

#### **Questions to think through while doing this JAM**

  - 💬 Ask Q: Explain why we need both Git AND Argo CD - what does each component do?

  - 💬 Ask Q: Show me the difference between manual kubectl apply vs GitOps deployment

  - 💬 Ask Q: What are the main benefits of GitOps over traditional deployment methods?

### **Getting Started**

- Find the Code Server link and password in the output properties and access the IDE. 
- Navigate to /home/ec2-user, open a terminal.
- Run `q login` to log in to Amazon Q CLI. *[Note: You will be prompted to select login method, choose `Use for Free with Builder ID` and open the URL provided in the terminal. If you already have one, enter the email associated with your Builder ID and choose Sign in. Otherwise, create a new AWS Builder ID using your personal email and follow the prompts to complete the sign-up process.]*
- Copy the AWS credentials from the `>_AWS_CLI` button at the top of the task description page.
- Paste the copied AWS credentials into the terminal. *[🚨 Note: Credentials expire after 10-15 minutes. If this happens, refresh the task description page, copy the new credentials from the >_AWS_CLI button, quit Q CLI  (`/quit`) and paste them in the terminal, restart Q CLI.]*
- Start the q session by entering `q chat` in the terminal
- Ask Q to Deploy the CloudFormation template present at `eks-cluster/eks-cluster.yaml`. After the stack deployment is completed (you can use Q to check the status of stack deployment), validate the EKS cluster deployment, and run the GitOps setup script at `../gitops-execution/gitops-setup.sh` with the help of Q.
- Capture the Git and Argo CD credentials from the output and save it to a notepad. You will need these in the next task.

*Note:*
- *If port forwarding stops working ask q "Run ./re-start-port-forward.sh"*
- *If you encounter any issues with script execution or app repository creation, you can resolve this by re-running the `gitops-setup.sh` script. Also try refreshing the AWS credentials and running the script again.*

### **Inventory**
- EKS Cluster CloudFormation template
- EC2 instance with Amazon Q Developer and EKS MCP Server
- GitOps deployment scripts prepared
- Code Server IDE

### **Services to Use**
- **Amazon Q Developer**
- **EKS MCP Server**
- **Amazon EKS**
- **AWS CloudFormation**

- The validation script should return a success message - if not, ask Q to troubleshoot


🚀 Infrastructure awakening complete! Ready to watch the GitOps giants come to life?

content:

Your GitOps infrastructure is alive, but it's just sleeping giants without purpose. Forge the sacred connection between your Git repository and Kubernetes through Argo CD.  This connection will create the mechanism where every Git commit automatically triggers deployments.

Establish the GitOps workflow by connecting Argo CD to the Git repository and deploy your first application through pure Git-driven automation.

- The script creates a Kubernetes Secret with your Git credentials for Argo CD to securely access your private repository. Ask Q to show you the gitea-repo secret that was created.

challengeTitle: Midnight Mayhem: GitOps to the Rescue
content:
### **Background**
The connection is established and your GitOps workflow is live! Now comes the exciting part - experiencing automated deployments in action. You're about to see how a 
simple Git commit instantly changes your running infrastructure without any manual work.

### **Your Mission**
Demonstrate GitOps automation by scaling an application through a Git commit and watch the magic of automatic synchronization unfold.

### **Getting Started**

- Open the Argo CD UI and confirm you can see the hello-gitops application with 2 replicas, then ask Q what the current state shows about your application deployment.
- Navigate to the app.yaml file in your app repository, change replicas from 2 to 3, and commit the change. 
- Return to Argo CD console and observe if the replicas automatically change to 3 *(click refresh if the update doesn't show instantly)*.
- For final verification, check the hello-gitops deployment in the EKS cluster to confirm it has changed from 2 to 3 replicas. 

### **Inventory**
- Amazon Q Developer
- EKS MCP Server

### **Services to Use**
- Amazon Q Developer
- EKS MCP Server

content:

content:
Everything works as expected using the current design and you are very proud of your work.
You manager comes in and she is very happy with the results. 

After reviewing the configuration with you, she mentions that in the near future the environment will need to be more resilient and will have to offer two or three availability zones.
This would mean more Suricata EC2 instances to maintain and manage.

You start to look for a managed firewall solution and discover **AWS Network Firewall**.

Before moving to a multi-AZ deployment, you decide to test **AWS Network Firewall**.

In this task, you need to **complete** the network configurations required to migrate from the existing solution using the **Gateway Laod Balancer** and the **Surica EC2 instances** to using **AWS Network Firewall** managed firewall service.

![](https://aws-jam-challenge-resources.s3.amazonaws.com/migrate-gwlb-to-nfw/architecture-candidate-nfw.png)

challengeTitle: AWS, Please Help me manage my Firewalls!
taskTitle: Migrate your existing Suricata rule to an AWS Network Firewall Suricata rule group
content:
In this task you want to migrate your existing rule to **AWS Network Firewall**.

You are required to:
- Create and attach a **Suricata compatible IPS rules** group to the  **Inspection-NFW** AWS Network Firewall
- Add the previously configured **drop** rule that was configured on the Suricata EC2 instance to **drop** all **HTTP** (not HTTPs) traffic going out to **amazon.com** (Not www.amazon.com).
- Make sure that **all other traffic** flowing through AWS Network Firewall is still **allowed to pass**

## Background

You will not be able to test the function. The only way to get the function to output the answer will be to create and utilize the correct invocation option. This "invoker" should allow Alice, the top analyst at GDI, to navigate to a specific web URL to get the function's output. ## Background
The clock is ticking! After discovering the broken deployments, Alex must quickly review the resources created from the previous deployment and implement security fixes. With multiple systems potentially exposed, there's no time to manually review each configuration. This is where the power of **[Amazon Q](https://aws.amazon.com/q/)**, *a generative AI–powered assistant*, proves valuable - its security assessment capabilities can significantly strengthen your defenses.

## Your Task
Leverage **Amazon Q** CLI, to identify and remediate security vulnerabilities in the existing Terraform infrastructure code. You'll need to perform security scans, understand the findings, and implement the necessary fixes to meet enterprise security standards.

### Step 2 – Security Assessment using Amazon Q CLI Chat
Use the `Amazon Q CLI chat` to perform the following actions:

- Ask Q to confirm whether `Terraform` is installed and available in the environment.
- Instruct Q to ***run a security scan using Checkov*** to identify any configuration vulnerabilities.

### Step 3 – Remediation & Validation using Amazon Q CLI Chat
Use the `Amazon Q CLI chat` to perform the following actions:

- Prompt Q to ***analyze and remediate*** the vulnerabilities identified in the previous scan.
- Ask Q to ***re-run the Checkov security scan*** to confirm that all issues have been resolved and to ***retrieve the corresponding Checkov scan IDs*** for validation.

## Background
Alex has *secured* the infrastructure, but the adventure isn’t over yet! **Managing Terraform** state is like guarding a magical artifact — *it ensures your infrastructure stays intact, avoids chaos, and allows your team to operate as a well-coordinated crew*.
#### Understanding Terraform State
Terraform state serves *three* crucial purposes:
1. **Resource Tracking**: Maps infrastructure code to real cloud resources
2. **Performance**: Helps determine what needs to be created, updated, or deleted
3. **Team Collaboration**: Enables multiple team members to work on the same infrastructure

By default, Terraform stores state locally in a `terraform.tfstate` file. However, for production environments, remote state storage and locking is essential for:
- Secure storage of sensitive information
- Team collaboration
- State locking to prevent concurrent modifications
- Backup and version control

## Your Task
Configure Terraform backend to store state remotely and implement state locking to prevent concurrent modifications. You'll use Amazon Q to understand and implement state management best practices.

## Getting Started
- Use Amazon Q to Configure terraform code to use a remote backend for ***state storage*** and ***state locking*** using pre-provisioned S3 bucket and DynamoDB table, for your recently created `basic-deployment-bucket` resource.
- Name of the pre-provisioned Amazon S3 bucket and Amazon DynamoDB table is provided in the `Output Properties` section. Use them to store the remote state file and state locking.
- Ensure state migration is successful and terraform operations work smoothly, along with this ensure the ***Key*** parameter in the backend file(backend.tf) is configured to use the following folder path `terraform-project/`.
- Use Amazon Q to guide you if you get stuck — it’s your magical assistant!
- **NOTE:** You need to initialize the terraform again to migrate the state from local to remote backend. Exit the Q CLI using `/quit` before running `terraform init`

## Inventory 
- A pre-provisioned S3 bucket for state storage: ***terraform-state-xxxxxxxxxxxx***
- A pre-provisioned DynamoDB table for state locking: ***terraform-lock-xxxxxxxxxxxx***
- Check `Output Properties` for the exact names

- Amazon DynamoDB

taskTitle: Document the Model: Add a Model Card
content:
### Background
The first thing you do is: Document the model.  This means, register all characteristics, features and decisions made during model creation, in an organized and reusable way.
To do this, you schedule a meeting with María, the Lead Data Scientist.  

These are your notes from the session:
-	Model was created in Amazon SageMaker Studio (as **AWS resource**, this means values like Model ARN, Model Artifacts and Inference environment are already set in the existng model)
-	It’s in it’s **2nd version**.
-	It’s a **Linear Regression** model, that takes features from 5000 movies of different years and genres, as well as the revenue generated by each of them. 
-	Uses an **Adaboost** algorithm that **minimizes Root Minimum Square Error (RMSE)**.
-	Features used from each movie were: 'popularity', 'runtime', 'release_year', 'release_month', 'original_language', 'genre' and ‘revenue’ (target)
-	María, the Lead Data Scientist was the **model creator**, but as **Model Owner** they plan to assign the Revenue Department.
-	The model was created because the Revenue Department (**the business stakeholders**) intend to solve the following business problem: *To estimate the approximate revenue that a movie will bring before its release, based on main movie attributes compared to other similar releases with similar characteristics*
-	The model **is intended** to be used as an aid to movie directors, producers and release designers to decide and plan possible changes to an upcoming movie before its final version (Like runtime, release date, design of release posters, etc.)
-	The model is **not intended** to be used for financial decisions. Neither to be used for planning future movies before they are even filmed on their majority. (Ethical Consideration)
-	The model will only work correctly, for the moment, in movies of in the language: English, Spanish, French, Chinese, Italian.  And genres: comedy, drama, romance, terror.  Other values or features will **affect model efficacy**.
-	The Data Science team estimates the model has a **medium risk** when being used because: The revenue value is not expected to be exact, but will provide an estimate “high/low” vision to producers, enough to make release decisions.

### Your Task
Create a SageMaker Model Card with the name *Movie-Revenue-Model-Card*, with the data you recollected from the meeting. (It can be in either **Draft or Approved** status)

### Getting Started

Find the **Model dashboard** feature under the **Governance** section in Amazon SageMaker menu.  Start filling the fields using your notes from the meeting.  
Have the Model name (*Movie-Revenue-Predictor-Model*) and the Training Job name (*TrainModelMoviesRevenueJob*) at hand, to have some infomation filled automatically when needed

### Inventory
- **SageMaker Model:** Movie-Revenue-Predictor-Model
- **SageMaker Training Job:** TrainModelMoviesRevenueJob

- The task will be finished automatically after meeting the task requirements. However, you can always check your progress by pressing the “Check my progress” button in the challenge details section.

taskTitle: Automate the Model: Configure Automatic Inference
content:
### Background
Amazing Job!  Now your model is not only documented, but correctly monitored in real time!  
Another important step of Machine Learning Operations (MLOps) and Data Governance is the automatization of some activities like retraining when an specific metrics gets stale, or trigger inference when new data becomes available.  
Assuming that you've already created an AWS StepFunction to call the model for predictions, use it to automate inference to new movie data that gets loaded to a specific S3 bucket folder.

Your final task will be to configure automatic execution of the AWS StepFunction **Movie-Revenue-Inference-SFN** as soon as new movie data gets loaded in the Amazon Simple Storage Service (S3) bucket **movie-revenue-artifacts-ACCOUNT_ID**, to generate the movie revenue predictions right away!

challengeTitle: Building PawsAndWhiskers: An Intelligent Pet Adoption Platform with Multi-Agent AI
taskTitle: Deploy AI-Powered PawsAndWhiskers Pet Adoption Platform
content:
## Background

Paws & Whiskers is a modern pet adoption platform that connects loving families with pets in need of homes. The platform demonstrates a cloud-native architecture featuring:

- **React-based frontend** for browsing available pets
- **Python FastAPI backend** for managing user accounts and adoption requests  
- **Advanced agentic AI core** powered by Strands Agents and Amazon Bedrock
- **Multi-agent orchestration** using A2A (Agent-to-Agent) protocol to coordinate specialized strands agents

The agentic core employs a sophisticated multi-agent system where a central **A2A Orchestrator** coordinates requests between specialized **Strands Agents**: a Knowledge Base Agent for general adoption guidance, a User Requests Agent for database queries, and a Pet Care Agent for detailed care plans. These agents communicate using the A2A protocol, creating an intelligent distributed system that provides comprehensive adoption assistance.

Your complete infrastructure has been pre-deployed using AWS CloudFormation, creating a fully configured cloud-native environment with all necessary AWS services and the application ready for configuration. Please check the inventory section for available components.

## Topics Covered

In this task, you will learn about:
- Deploying containerized applications using Docker Compose
- Understanding multi-agent AI architectures with Strands agent and A2A protocol
- Testing cloud-native application components
- Integrating AI chat capabilities with web applications

## Technical Knowledge Prerequisites

- Basic understanding of AWS services (EC2, DynamoDB, Application Load Balancer)
- Familiarity with Docker and containerization concepts
- Basic command line navigation and Docker Compose usage
- Understanding of web application architecture (frontend/backend separation)

## Category Difficulty

**300 - Advanced**: This task requires basic AWS knowledge and Docker experience but provides guided instructions for all steps.

## Your Task

Deploy the containerized application on EC2, and test all key features. Through this task, you'll understand how the **A2A Orchestrator** routes requests to the **Knowledge Base Agent** for AI processing using the A2A protocol.

### Task Steps:

1. **Connect to your EC2 instance** and navigate to `/opt/pawsandwhiskers-app`
2. **Inspect the Knowledge Base Agent** to understand the strands agent implementation:
   - Navigate to `knowledgebase-agent/` directory and examine the `knowledgebase_agent.py` file
   - This contains the Strands agent with built-in pet adoption knowledge base
   - From the code check the Bedrock model that is being used
3. **Deploy the containerized application** using Docker Compose to observe strands Orchestrator agent coordinating with the Knowledge Base Agent
   - *Hint: If there are issues, clean up your docker cache and run the following command*
   ```bash
   # Stop existing containers, build and start all services
   docker-compose down && docker-compose up -d --build
   
   # Restart frontend container
   docker-compose up -d --build frontend
   ```
4. **Find your Application Load Balancer URL** provided in the outputs section of this page (task page) and test the deployed application
   - Find the application URL in the output section
   
   ![Output section](https://aws-jam-challenge-resources.s3.amazonaws.com/modernizepawsandwhiskers/OutputPropertiesALB.png)
5. **Verify all features** including user authentication, pet browsing, and AI chat functionality. Create a user and request adoption of a dog, cat and a bunny.
6. **Test AI Chat Integration**:
   - **Access the Chat Feature** (look for chat bubble to right of the footer)
   - **Test AI Responses** with these sample questions (Chat that is functional with current configurations, keep it within this scope):
     - "What are adoption fees?"
     - "How do I adopt a pet?"
     - "What are your facility hours?"
   
     **Chat that does not work yet**:
     - "What are my adoption requests"
     - "Tell me about dog care"

## Task Validation

Enter the Bedrock Model used by knowledgebase-agent in the text field upon completion to validate the task.

## Getting Started

The complete infrastructure has already been deployed to your AWS account, including:

```
┌─────────────────┐    ┌──────────────────┐    ┌─────────────────────┐
│   React UI      │    │  Python FastAPI  │    │    Orchestrator.    │
│   (Frontend)    │◄──►│    (Backend)     │◄──►│   (Strands Agent)   │─────┐
│   Port 80       │    │   Port 5000      │    │      Port 8080      │     | 
└─────────────────┘    └──────────────────┘    └─────────────────────┘     | 
         │                       │                       │                 |
         │                       │                       ▼                 | 
         │                       │              ┌─────────────────┐        | 
         │                       │              │ Knowledge Base  │        |
         │                       │              │ (Strands Agent) │        |                 
         │                       │              │   Port 8081     │        |                     
         │                       │              └─────────────────┘        |   
         │                       │                       │                 |
         │                       │                       ▼                 |
         │                       │              ┌─────────────────┐        |
         │                       │              │ Amazon Bedrock  │        |
         │                       │              │     (LLM)       │◄───────┘ 
         │                       │              └─────────────────┘
         │                       │                       
         ▼                       ▼                       
┌─────────────────┐    ┌──────────────────┐    
│ Application     │    │    DynamoDB      │    
│ Load Balancer   │    │   (3 Tables)     │    
└─────────────────┘    └──────────────────┘    
```

## Inventory

Your pre-deployed environment includes:

### AWS Infrastructure
- **VPC**: Custom VPC with public/private subnets across 2 availability zones
- **EC2 Auto Scaling Group**: t3.medium instances running the containerized application
- **Application Load Balancer**: Internet-facing ALB distributing traffic to your application
- **DynamoDB Tables**: Three tables for users, adoption requests, and feedback

content:
## Background

Building on Task 1's successful deployment, you'll now enhance the Paws & Whiskers platform with a specialized User Requests Agent. This dedicated strands agent handles user-specific queries about adoption requests, providing personalized responses by directly accessing the DynamoDB database.

The User Requests Agent works alongside the existing Knowledge Base Agent, coordinated through the Orchestrator Agent to create a multi-agent system where different types of queries are intelligently routed to the most appropriate strands agent. This architecture demonstrates how modern AI systems using Strands agent and A2A protocol can seamlessly distribute work across specialized agents.

The User Requests Agent is specifically designed to handle queries like "Show me my adoption requests" and "What's the status of my applications?" by connecting directly to DynamoDB and formatting user-specific data into friendly, readable responses.

## Topics Covered

In this task, you will learn about:
- AI Multi-agent system architecture using Strands agent and A2A protocol

The Pet Care Agent goes beyond simple Q&A by providing structured, actionable pet care information. It can deliver essential care guidelines, emergency contacts, and breed-specific advice - all powered by AI and coordinated through Strands agent and A2A protocol.

This completes your journey from a single-agent system to a 3-agent orchestration platform, demonstrating modern AI architecture patterns used in the pet care applications.

taskTitle: Identify and fix CFN_NAG validation issue
content: #### Background AWS CloudFormation template has a `security issue` because of which it is failing the pipeline stage when run through AWS CodePipeline. CodePipeline has a Build phase using AWS CodeBuild which performs security checks on the CloudFormation template using `cfn_nag`. CodePipeline is being sourced from AWS Codecommit repository and template is placed inside the `src` folder #### Your Task You need to identify and fix the security issues. You can investigate the AWS CodeBuild output from AWS Console. Upon investigation, when you identify the issue, commit the changes on the main branch. The `AWS CodePipeline` can be triggered manually via [**Release Changes**] post fixing the template and by committing the change on the CloudFormation template. #### Getting Started - Click on Open AWS Console - Navigate to CodePipeline Service - Click on a Jam-Challenge-Code-Pipeline - Check the `failing` stage i.e., `CFN_NAG_CHECK` #### Inventory Your AWS account has been provisioned with the following resources: - AWS CodePipeline: The pipeline which is running the Security Checks, refer `Jam-Challenge-Code-Pipeline` - AWS CodeCommit: The repository which stores CloudFormation tempates , refer `Jam-Challenge` - Security Tool: cfn-nag #### Task Validation Task will be validated automatically once the AWS CodePiepeline `CFN_NAG_CHECK` stage turns **Green**

challengeTitle: Building Multi-Agent Investment Firms with Strands SDK
content:
## Background
A stock trading team typically consists of analysts, traders, and risk managers. In our system, each team member is represented by an LLM powered by the Strands Agent framework. The goal is to build a system within a limited timeframe that simulates the collaborative decision-making process of a real trading team.

Strands Agent is a convenient framework that enables easy creation of AI agents. We have prepared specialized tools that you can use to create finance associate agents.

## Your Tasks

### Background:

![VPC Architecture](https://aws-jam-challenge-resources.s3.amazonaws.com/multicast-with-transit-gateway/1.0.0-dev/JamArchitecture-Task1.png "VPC Architecture")

### Getting Started:

You have been asked to make sure multicast communication can work across multiple subnets in different availability zones.  
Within this environment there are three EC2 Instances running within Jam VPC but in different subnets.
You can access all instances using **ONLY** SSM [Session Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/session-manager-working-with-sessions-start.html#start-ec2-console). You can use `sudo` to run privileged commands or to become `root`.

On each instance you will find a tool called `omping` installed. This tool can be used to test multicast communication between instances.

On the left panel at **Output Properties**, you will find `MulticastTestCommand`.

![omping command](https://aws-jam-challenge-resources.s3.amazonaws.com/multicast-with-transit-gateway/1.0.0-dev/Jam-Task1-Clue1.png "omping command")

Your task is:
* Open a session to each EC2 instance using [Session Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/session-manager-working-with-sessions-start.html#start-ec2-console). On each session use command `omping` to check multicast network traffic. Get the command from the `Output Properties`, it is identified as `MulticastTestCommand`

You will notice `omping` only shows you unicast lines. Not multicast. You will have 100% loss on multicast. Which means multicast is not working on your VPC.

Keep it running for some seconds. After a while press CTRL+C to quit.  
When you press CTRL+C it will show you statistics from all other IPs.

In example below you can see CTRL+C as `^C` and statistics as 4 last lines.  
Please note that you will have 100% loss on multicast.

### Background:
VPC itself does not support multicast. For multicast to works is necessary to use [AWS Transit Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/what-is-transit-gateway.html).

![VPC Architecture](https://aws-jam-challenge-resources.s3.amazonaws.com/multicast-with-transit-gateway/1.0.0-dev/JamArchitecture-Task2.png "VPC Architecture")

### Getting Started:
A transit gateway is a network transit hub that you can use to interconnect your virtual private clouds (VPCs) and on-premises networks. As your cloud infrastructure expands globally, inter-Region peering connects transit gateways together using the AWS Global Infrastructure. Your data is automatically encrypted and never travels over the public internet.

You can enable multicast on a transit gateway, and then create a transit gateway multicast domain that allows multicast traffic to be sent from your multicast source to multicast group members over VPC attachments that you associate with the domain.

**Transit gateway attachments to a VPC**  
When you attach a VPC to a transit gateway, you must specify one subnet from each Availability Zone to be used by the transit gateway to route traffic. Specifying one subnet from an Availability Zone enables traffic to reach resources in every subnet in that Availability Zone.

To support multicast, you need to create transit gateway and attach it to `Jam` VPC.  
Make sure you enable multicast support, by default it is not selected. **You can't enable it later!**

If transit gateway will be used only to support multicast you don't need to worry about `Amazon side Autonomous System Number (ASN)` or any other configuration. You can keep them as is.

Your task is:
* Create transit gateway and wait for its state to be `Available`
* Create transit gateway attachment using `Jam` VPC and subnets `Subnet1`, `Subnet2` and `Subnet3`. Wait for its state to be `Available` (be patient!)

----
#### ❌ 👮 Attention!
Please **ignore [default VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/default-vpc.html)**, the one with CIDR `172.31.0.0/16`. Nothing is required about *default* VPC on this Jam challenge. Always use a VPC called `Jam`!

----

### Task Validation:
To complete this task, you need to:
* Create transit gateway with `Multicast support` selected
* Create transit gateway attachment using `Jam` VPC and subnets `Subnet1`, `Subnet2` and `Subnet3`

You can click on `Check my progress` button or just wait and it will validate automatically.

### Background:
Now that you have transit gateway you need to create a [multicast domain](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/tgw-multicast-overview.html).

![VPC Architecture](https://aws-jam-challenge-resources.s3.amazonaws.com/multicast-with-transit-gateway/1.0.0-dev/JamArchitecture-Task3.png "VPC Architecture")

### Getting Started:
Multicast is a communication protocol used for delivering a single stream of data to multiple receiving computers simultaneously. Transit Gateway supports routing multicast traffic between subnets of attached VPCs, and it serves as a multicast router for instances sending traffic destined for multiple receiving instances.

**Considerations**  
* A subnet can only be in one multicast domain.
* Multicast routing is not supported over AWS Direct Connect, Site-to-Site VPN, or peering attachments.
* When the multicast source and destination are in the same VPC, you cannot use security group referencing to set the destination security group to accept traffic from the source's security group.

**IGMPv2 support**  
IGMPv2 support enables dynamic membership management for a multicast domain. Hosts in associated subnets in VPCs can join and leave multicast groups on demand using IGMPv2 protocol messages.

Your task is:
* Create transit gateway multicast domain and wait for its state to be `Available`
* Associate multicast domain with `Subnet1`, `Subnet2`, `Subnet3` and wait all associations have state `Available`

----
#### ❌ 👮 Attention!
Please **ignore [default VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/default-vpc.html)**, the one with CIDR `172.31.0.0/16`. Nothing is required about *default* VPC on this Jam challenge. Always use a VPC called `Jam`!

----

### Task Validation:
To complete this task, you need to:
* Create transit gateway multicast domain with `IGMPv2 support` selected
* Create transit gateway multicast domain association with `Subnet1`, `Subnet2`, `Subnet3`

You can click on `Check my progress` button or just wait and it will validate automatically.

### Background:
You are almost there, you already have everything set on Transit Gateway. Your instances have a Security Group, but no inbound rules!

![VPC Architecture](https://aws-jam-challenge-resources.s3.amazonaws.com/multicast-with-transit-gateway/1.0.0-dev/JamArchitecture-Task4.png "VPC Architecture")

### Getting Started:
When you enable multicast on a transit gateway, it acts as a multicast router. When you add a subnet to a multicast domain, we send all multicast traffic to the transit gateway that is associated with that multicast domain.

**Security Group**  
Security group rules operate at the instance level. They can be applied to both inbound and outbound multicast traffic. The behavior is the same as with unicast traffic. For all group member instances, you must allow inbound traffic from the group source.

For IGMP multicast traffic, you must have the following inbound rules at a minimum. The remote host is the host sending the multicast traffic. **You can't specify a security group as the source of the UDP inbound rule.**

Your task is:
* Change security group called `Jam` to add correct inbound rules
* You don't need to change anything on outbound!
* Use VPC CIDR as source for UDP
* Use `All UDP` as `Type` for UDP rule

More information on [Multicast routing](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/how-multicast-works.html) documentation.

----
#### ❌ 👮 Attention!
Please **ignore [default VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/default-vpc.html)**, the one with CIDR `172.31.0.0/16`. Nothing is required about *default* VPC on this Jam challenge. Always use a VPC called `Jam`!

This Jam challenge uses `All UDP` just to facilitate the learning process, so you don't need to know which port `omping` uses!

----

### Task Validation:
To complete this task, you need to:
* Change security group called `Jam` to add correct inbound rules.

**Considerations**  
* You don't need to change anything on outbound!
* You don't need to change anything on Network ACLs!
* Use VPC CIDR as source for UDP rule. It **MUST** match exactly, otherwise task will not validate!
* Use `All UDP` as `Type` for UDP rule

You can click on `Check my progress` button or just wait and it will validate automatically.

### Background:
You fixed everything outside your instances. Now it is time to fix instances and see multicast working!

![VPC Architecture](https://aws-jam-challenge-resources.s3.amazonaws.com/multicast-with-transit-gateway/1.0.0-dev/JamArchitecture-Task4.png "VPC Architecture")

### Getting Started:
Transit Gateways support IGMP version 2 and not the later version 3. Therefore, it is critical that any systems which are expected to receive multicast traffic are configured to support IGMPv2. For Linux, as in the case of this Jam challenge, this is done by setting the corresponding kernel parameters. The following command shows how:

```shell
sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.conf.eth0.force_igmp_version=2
```

You can check the version it is configured with command below:
```shell
[root@ip-10-0-0-92 ~]# cat /proc/net/igmp
Idx     Device    : Count Querier       Group    Users Timer    Reporter
1       lo        :     1      V3
                                010000E0     1 0:00000000               0
2       eth0      :     1      V2
                                010000E0     1 0:00000000               0
```

----

##### ❌ 👮 Attention!
Change kernel parameter in this way will not make it persistent, and this command or similar must therefore be run each boot time.

----

Your task is:
* Configure all 3 instances to support IGMPv2
* Run `omping` command from `MulticastTestCommand` on all 3 instances in parallel at the same time. It takes some time, be patience!

Keep it running. You should see it running like below:
```shell
10.0.0.92 :   unicast, seq=21, size=69 bytes, dist=0, time=2.106ms
10.0.0.92 : multicast, seq=21, size=69 bytes, dist=0, time=2.113ms
10.0.2.79 :   unicast, seq=20, size=69 bytes, dist=0, time=1.330ms
10.0.2.79 : multicast, seq=20, size=69 bytes, dist=0, time=1.715ms
10.0.0.92 :   unicast, seq=22, size=69 bytes, dist=0, time=2.117ms
10.0.0.92 : multicast, seq=22, size=69 bytes, dist=0, time=2.125ms
10.0.2.79 :   unicast, seq=21, size=69 bytes, dist=0, time=1.274ms
10.0.2.79 : multicast, seq=21, size=69 bytes, dist=0, time=1.357ms
```

If you don't see lines with `multicast`, like examples below, it is wrong.

```shell
 10.0.2.79 :   unicast, seq=1, size=69 bytes, dist=0, time=0.865ms
 10.0.0.92 :   unicast, seq=2, size=69 bytes, dist=0, time=2.569ms
 10.0.2.79 :   unicast, seq=2, size=69 bytes, dist=0, time=0.954ms
 10.0.0.92 :   unicast, seq=3, size=69 bytes, dist=0, time=2.466ms
```

```shell
10.0.0.92 : waiting for response msg
10.0.2.79 : waiting for response msg
10.0.0.92 : waiting for response msg
10.0.2.79 : waiting for response msg
```

Also please check your transit gateway multicast domain groups.  
You should see ENIs from your 3 instances on group IP address `224.0.0.1` and `224.10.10.10`.

See an example below  
![transit gateway multicast domain groups](https://aws-jam-challenge-resources.s3.amazonaws.com/multicast-with-transit-gateway/1.0.0-dev/transit-gateway-multicast-domain-groups.png "transit gateway multicast domain groups")

Just keep it running on all 3 instances and task will validate automatically. It can take up-to 5 minutes.

content: ## Background To verify domain name routing with ALB, we have prepared the following resources. - VPC: `JamVPC` - ALB: `JamALB` (This is an internal load balancer for internal use.) - Target groups: `target-cat`, `target-dog` - EC2 instance: `Client` (EC2 instance to test ALB access.) We want to use subdomains of `example.test` for ALB, such as `cat.example.test` or `dog.example.com`. We would like to use AWS solutions to reduce settings like /etc/hosts or /etc/resolve.conf for each client in VPCs. ## Your Task Check the domain name of `JamALB` (ex. `xxx.xxx.elb.amazonaws.com`). You can check `JamALB` response by connecting to EC2 instance with Session Manager and exec `curl -k https://xxx.xxx.elb.amazonaws.com` command, but we can only access `JamALB` with this domain name. Your task is to allow clients in `JamVPC` to access `JamALB` with the domains `cat.example.test` and `dog.example.test`.Then ensure route requests based on the host name. This is the final architecture overview. ## Getting Started Please exec `curl -k https://xxx.xxx.elb.amazonaws.com` command from `Client` instance to confirm connection. ## Inventory - VPC: `JamVPC` - ALB: `JamALB` - EC2 instance: `Client` ## Services You Should Use - ALB - Route 53 ## Task Validation This task will be automatically marked as completed when: - We can request to `https://cat.example.test` from clients in `JamVPC`, and the request is reached to `JamALb` and routed to `target-cat` target group. - We can request to `https://dog.example.test` from clients in `JamVPC`, and the request is reached to `JamALb` and routed to `target-dog` target group. - `JamALb` HTTPS:443 listener default action is set fixed response (response code: `404`, response body: `Not Found`). - You have following DNS records. - record name: `example.test`, type: `NS` - record name: `cat.example.test`, type: `A` using alias record - record name: `dog.example.test`, type: `A` using alias record Note: When checking the request from the Client to the ALB, it may take a little time for the DNS settings to actually reflect in the VPC. However, if the correct settings are made, the challenge will clear. Additionally, you can always check your progress by clicking on the _Check my progress_ button on the Challenge Details screen. ---

Background

As the security engineer for a large project that involves processing personal, sensitive, and highly valuable data, your role is to ensure the integrity and confidentiality of this information. You work closely with the project team to identify and mitigate potential security risks, implement appropriate safeguards, and ensure compliance with relevant laws and regulations.

As you sit at your desk, you receive an urgent call from the security operations center (SOC) team. The consultant informs you that during the course of a recent security team investigation, an IP address was detected that doesn't belong to the production network segment. This news sends a shiver down your spine, as you know that such a breach could potentially compromise sensitive information and put the entire project at risk.

Inventory

  • VPCs

  • EC2

Getting Started

Anomaly detection mechanisms within the production environment have flagged a concerning observation: a known EC2 instance appears to be communicating with another EC2 instance belonging to the same organization but outside the expected environment. Further investigation is warranted to determine the nature and intent of this communication, and to evaluate any potential security risks posed by these actions. Embark on a quest to discover the ultimate VPC feature that can unravel the mystery and enhance the discovery phase!

Your Task

Your primary goal is to use an AWS solution to create an analysis to identify the origin of incoming communication. This will enable you to determine how many findings are associated and where it is coming from.

Task Validation

To obtain the answer, you need to identify the AWS solution which can create the analyzer to discover how many findings are associated between the unknown environment with production instance environment. The answer need to be the initials of the service name using Capital Letter and the number of findings discovered. Example (Initials+Findings): Let's assume you used the VPC Flow Logs service and discovered 50 findings, the answer would be: VFL50.

HINT: Don't waste your time, please remember that activating VPC Flow Logs is not allowed for your project. This is because has specific budget constraints and enabling it would incur additional expenses. Find the best service to resolve the task.

As experts in your field, we trust that you have the necessary knowledge and expertise to identify the root cause and resolve it. We'll provide you with the necessary clues and guidance to help you if you want.

HINT: The result of the previous task is not only about finding, it helps identify where the communication originated and where it is going, which is important for understanding where this communication is taking place to resolve and complete the task. Only misconfigured routes needs to be deleted, understand the findings in the previous task and resolve the task.

#### Background As a service provider, you are troubleshooting errors for one of your ShareZone customers. The customer has recently made changes to their security posture and now they are unable to access the webpage for your service receiving connection timeout errors. Your customer asks you to resolve the issue by providing access to an EC2 instance in their Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC) and their VPC configuration. In this challenge, you have access two VPCs - your own (Service Provider) and the customers (Service Consumer). Here are some details about the design: **Service Provider:** - The application is hosted across three Amazon EC2 instances in `VPC B - Service Provider` with one EC2 instance per Availability Zone (AZ). - Ingress traffic is load balanced using a Network Load Balancer, which is registered to the AWS Endpoint Service in `VPC B - Service Provider`. **Service Consumer:** - The AWS Endpoint Interface is deployed across three Elastic Network Interfaces (ENIs) in separate private subnets, each in a different Availability Zone within `VPC A - Service Consumer`. - Use the `ConsumerInstance` in `VPC A - Service Consumer` to test connectivity to the Endpoint Interfaces. #### Architecture Diagram (Click image to open in new tab) # #### Your Task To successfully complete the task, you must resolve the connectivity issue through the two Endpoint Interfaces. You should accomplish the following: - Receive a 200 OK HTML response code when cURL to the `EndpointInterface` domain is issued. Try running the command multiple times to ensure you are getting a 200 OK from *both* the Endpoint Interface IPs. Note: The `EndpointInterfaceDomain` DNS name will resolve 2 out of the 3 Endpoint Interface IPs currently. *You will address this problem separately in the next task while working on the Service Provider configuration.* Here is a sample output you should expect to see indicating the problem is fixed. (Click image to open in a new tab)
#### Getting Started - Use Session Manager initiated in the EC2 console to connect to the `ConsumerInstance` Amazon EC2 instance. - For the first task, try using `dig EndpointInterfaceDomain` to check the DNS resolution for the Endpoint Interface Domain name. *(Reminder - it should only resolve 2 IPs currently. This will be addressed in task 2.)* - Next, issue `curl -Iv http://EndpointInterfaceDomain` and check the response. - You can find the `EndpointInterfaceDomain` under **Output Properties** on the left side of this page. - *cURL stands for "Client URL" and is used to transfer data using a URL.* # - Additional considerations: - Use AWS best practices while configuring firewall rules. - Firewall rules should not allow all protocol and port traffic. - Think from security perspective at the instance level and subnet level.
#### Inventory ###### **Service Consumer** - **VPC**: Name - **Service Consumer VPC**, CIDR - 10.0.0.0/16 - **Subnets** - Subnet 1: Name - ConsumerPrivateSubnet1, CIDR - 10.0.1.0/24 - Subnet 2: Name - ConsumerPrivateSubnet2, CIDR - 10.0.2.0/24 - Subnet 3: Name - ConsumerPrivateSubnet3, CIDR - 10.0.3.0/24 # - **Consumer Endpoint Interface:** - Name - Refer to the value of `EndpointInterfaceId` in **Output Properties** - Endpoint Domain Name - Refer to the value of `EndpointInterfaceDomain ` in **Output Properties** - The Endpoint Interface has 3 Elastic Network Interfaces (ENIs), 1 in each of the Consumer Private Subnets. # - **Consumer Instance:** - Name - ConsumerInstance - Private IP: 10.0.0.11 - AWS Systems Manager Agent (SSM Agent) is already installed.
#### Services you should use: - Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) - Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2)
#### Task Validation There are three configuration changes needed to complete this task. Once these changes are made, you should be able to see a '200 OK' response for the cURL command from 2 of the Endpoint Interface IPs. The task will automatically mark itself as complete within a few minutes of seeing the successful cURL response. You may hit the **Check my progress** button as well, once you believe the solution has been implemented. Note: The task will **NOT** officially be marked as complete if you have allowed access from the Internet (0.0.0.0/0) in the inbound rules.

content:

Additionally, the Network Load Balancer (NLB) should distribute traffic evenly across healthy targets residing in all three availability zones. Refer to the value of `NLBDomainName` in **Output Properties** for the DNS name. - **Target Group**: - Name - **ProviderTargetGroup** # - **Network Load Balancer Targets** - Name - TargetInstance1, Subnet - ProviderPrivateSubnet1, Private IP: 20.0.1.10 - Name - TargetInstance2, Subnet - ProviderPrivateSubnet2, Private IP: 20.0.2.10 - Name - TargetInstance3, Subnet - ProviderPrivateSubnet3, Private IP: 20.0.3.10

taskTitle: Team! Let me access the instance first
content:
#### Background
---
In order to investigate the Windows patching issue, production server details are shared with John, however he must be able to first connect the Windows EC2 instance via Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP). But while attempting to connect to the server, he observed that EC2 instance lacks Internet connectivity. To access the instance from his home/office, John requires to configure the network settings which will enable RDP as well as internet access to the given EC2 instance.


#### Your Task
---
As John, your task is to:

* Identify the affected Windows EC2 instance
* Enable RDP and internet access from the instance's Security Group
* Connect the affected EC2 instance via RDP

#### Getting Started
---
* **Identify the affected EC2 instance** - From the EC2 Management Console, identify the affected EC2 instance by referring the Instance ID provided in the **Output Properties** section. 

* **Enable RDP and Internet Access** - Please ensure that RDP access to the affected instance is allowed from your source network by having the concerned inbound rule added in the associated Security group (specify **Source** as **"My IP"**). Additionally check if the Internet traffic is allowed in the outbound rule of the same Security Group.

* **Connect the affected EC2 instance via RDP** - After enabling RDP and Internet access, connect the EC2 Windows instance via RDP client from your source Windows machine (for macOS download Microsoft Remote Desktop application from AppStore) using its public IPv4 address which can be determined from the EC2 Management console by referring to the provided EC2 Instance ID and user's login credentials in the **Output Properties** section.

#### Inventory
---
* Windows EC2 Instance named `Production-Server`.
* Security Group attached to the EC2 instance named `Production-SecurityGroup`.
* Check **Output Properties** section for EC2 Instance ID, Security Group ID and login credentials.

#### Services You Should Use
---
* Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2)
* Access via Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) client

#### Task Validation
---
Once you've enabled RDP and Internet access to the given EC2 instance, please connect the same via RDP using provided login credentials from your allowed **source address**. If you can successfully connect, then proceed to validate this task by entering your **source public IPv4 address** in the input field, for which you've allowed the RDP access in the instance's Security group.

For example, if your source public IPv4 address from where you're able to connect the instance via RDP is `54.32.12.34` then please enter **"your-public-ipv4-address/32"** in the input field of this task like: `54.32.12.34/32`

`!IMPORTANT NOTES!` 
* The source IPv4 address you enter in the task's input field must be the one for which you've allowed RDP access in the instance's Security group.
* If you're connected to a VPN connection, please ensure the IPv4 address picked by **Source** as **My IP** option in the instance's Security Group is correct one. 
* If you encounter any RDP issue, then disconnect from VPN, modify the inbound rule again to choose **Source** as **My IP** option and then retry the RDP connection.
* After this task gets successfully validated, the EC2 instance would be automatically rebooted so please reconnect if your RDP connection drops.

taskTitle: Ah! why it has to be always the Windows update?
content:
#### Background
---
After getting access to the EC2 instance, next John has to determine the possible cause behind Windows patching failure and mitigate it. John has been informed about the following setup:

1) An **AWS Systems Manager** State Manager Associaton named **Production-Patching** is configured for the concerned production server to periodically perform Windows patching using **AWS-RunPatchBaseline** Run command document.
2) This association must be in `Success` state but currently its status is marked as `Failed`.
3) It was reported that some recent Windows update configuration changes around WSUS server made at the OS level of the instance, has caused the Windows update patching to fail when invoked by above State Manager Association named **Production-Patching**.
4) You can check for yourself, when you go to **AWS Systems Manager > Under Node Management > State Manager > Production-Patching**, click on **Apply association now** button to trigger the patching on the instance and wait for sometime to complete its execution, getting failed state at the end.
5) Due to this failure, instance is marked as `Non-compliant` if you check Compliance report on **AWS Systems Manager > Under Node Management > Patch Manager > Dashboard > Compliance report** or Compliance on **AWS Systems Manager > Under Node Management > Compliance** console.

`NOTE:`
After last reboot of the instance, you might see **Production-Patching** association still applying and would be in progress state however if you wait for sometime, it would eventually fail.

#### Your Task
---
As John, your task is to:

* Investigate and determine the possible cause behind Windows patching failure
* Fix the patching issue and re-apply the association to get it into `Success` state

#### Getting Started
---
* Go to State Manager Console **AWS Systems Manager > Under Node Management > State Manager > Associations.**
* You'll find an Association named **Production-Patching** with status as `Failed`. Click on the Association ID to check the details.
* Go to the last tab named **Execution history** to see previous patching execution attempts. 
* Click on the **Execution id** to get more details on the execution summary and output.

After gathering information on last failed patching attempt, please connect the EC2 instance via RDP and start your investigation at the OS end around possible reasons behind Windows update failure as per reported concerns.

Post you mitigate the concerns at OS level, go to State Manager console and then re-apply the association by clicking on the **Apply association now** button on the top right. It will trigger the Windows update and after sometimes it will return the state of the patching whether it succeeded based on the fix you made at the OS end.

#### Inventory
---
* Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) Windows Instance named **Production-Server**.
* A State Manager Association named **Production-Patching**.
* Check **Output Properties** section for Patch Association ID, EC2 Instance ID and login credentials.

#### Services You Should Use
---
* Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2)
* AWS Systems Manager

#### Task Validation
---
The task will be automatically completed once the concerned **Production-Patching** association enters into `Success` state. In addition you can always check your progress by pressing the **Check my progress** button in the challenge details screen.

#### Background
---
After successfully mitigating the Windows patching issue, John wondered that the concerned production server is still not marked as `Compliant` over **AWS Systems Manager > Under Node Management > Compliance** dashboard.

Later John found that the EC2 instance would be marked as `Compliant` if all instance's associations are in `Success` state. Further checking this requirement, he found that there exist another State Manager association which is in `Failed` state. The details are as follow:

1) A State Manager Associaton named **Production-Configuration** is provisioned to apply OS level configuration changes remotely using **AWS-RunPowerShellScript** Run command document.
2) This association must be in `Success` state but currently its status is marked as `Failed`.
3) It was reported that a recent deployed Windows configuration has failed to apply when invoked by above State Manager Association.
4) You can check for yourself, when you go to **AWS Systems Manager > Under Node Management > State Manager > Production-Configuration**, click on Associatoion id and check the output details.
5) Due to this failure, instance is marked as `Non-compliant` if you check the Compliance under **AWS Systems Manager > Under Node Management > Compliance** console.


#### Your Task
---
As John, your task is to:

* Review the **Production-Configuration** association execution output and try to determine the possible cause behind its failure
* Fix the concerns and then re-apply the **Production-Configuration** association to get it into `Success` state.

#### Getting Started
---
* Go to State Manager Console **AWS Systems Manager > Under Node Management > State Manager > Associations.**
* You'll find an Association named **Production-Configuration** with status as `Failed`. Click on the Association ID to check the details.
* Go to the last tab named **Execution history** to see the last failed attempts to deploy OS level configurations. 
* Click on the **Execution id** to get more details on the execution summary and output.

In the output section for the last execution, you'd find the possible root cause behind its failure. Follow the instructions and make the necessary changes to finally re-apply the **Production-Configuration** association to get it into `Success` state.

#### Inventory
---
* Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) Windows Instance named **Production-Server**.
* A State Manager Association named **Production-Configuration**.
* Check **Output Properties** section for Configuration Association ID, EC2 Instance ID and login credentials.

#### Services You Should Use
---
* Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2)
* AWS Systems Manager

#### Task Validation
---
The task will be automatically completed once the concerned **Production-Configuration** association enters into `Success` state. In addition you can always check your progress by pressing the **Check my progress** button in the challenge details screen.

taskTitle: First Mission: Identify the Parrot You Intend to Rescue
content:
### Background: As an elite AWS Security Professional, you're about to embark on a high-stakes rescue mission. Your mission is to identify and liberate a parrot in distress! This isn't just any ordinary bird-saving operation. The parrot has sent out an SOS link, signaling for your help, and it's up to you to follow the digital breadcrumbs. Your task is to fix permission issues using the principle of least privilege, ensuring that only the right parrot gains freedom while keeping the sneaky bad parrots securely locked away. The first task is to: **Identify the Parrot** - Fix permissions to discover which parrot you need to rescue The clock is ticking, and the fate of this parrot is in your hands! Remember—security first! Reinforce protections as you go to prevent the wrong birds from escaping. It's time to prove your AWS security prowess and complete the mission!

You must fix the PUT request permission issue between the Lambda function and S3 bucket. To complete this challenge, you must: 1. Access the API Endpoint URL given to you 2. challengeTitle: Only That Parrot Can Escape: Mastering IAM, RCP, and SCP Policies with Least Privilege
taskTitle: Final Mission: Unlock the Parrot Cage and Rescue the parrot
content:
### Background:

Now that you've found the magic link to the parrot cage, you face the final challenge: unlocking the cage itself. The cage requires two security policy to open—properly, you need to configure Service Control Policies (SCPs) and Resource Control Policies (RCPs).

In AWS Organizations, these policies are crucial for comprehensive security management:

- **Service Control Policies (SCPs)** define the maximum permissions for IAM users and roles within an AWS organization, ensuring accounts comply with organizational access guidelines.

- **Resource Control Policies (RCPs)** manage permissions on AWS resources themselves, establishing data perimeters by restricting external access at scale.

Your task is to implement both policy types to enforce proper security controls while maintaining the principle of least privilege.

**Objective: Unlock the Parrot Cage** - Configure SCPs and RCPs to implement essential security controls

The final rescue phase has begun! Apply your AWS security expertise to unlock the cage and free the parrot safely.

### Getting Started:

You need to configure two key security policies to enforce specific controls:

1. **Service Control Policy (SCP):** Restrict all AWS service usage exclusively to the `us-east-1` region.

2. **Resource Control Policy (RCP):** Implement S3 bucket security controls to:
   - Enforce a minimum TLS version of 1.2 for all connections
   - Mandate KMS encryption for all uploaded objects

### Your Task:

As the AWS Security Professional, you are going to start with:

1. Visit the Magic URL you get from Task 2 and access the page
2. Edit the Service Control Policy (SCP) to restrict service usage to the `us-east-1` region only
3. Edit the Resource Control Policy (RCP) to enforce TLS 1.2 and KMS encryption for S3 buckets
4. Apply the principle of least privilege in all policy modifications
5. Complete both policy implementations to unlock the cage and rescue the parrot

To successfully complete this challenge, ensure each policy implements the exact security controls specified.

### Inventory:

* **AWS Organizations**: But you only need to access task Magic URL to perform the edit, no need to access the actual service.



### Task Validation:

After implementing the security policies correctly:

1. The parrot cage will unlock
2. The Secret Code will appear in the Magic URL
3. You can validate that:
   - All AWS service requests outside `us-east-1` are denied
   - S3 connections require TLS 1.2 or higher
   - All S3 object uploads require KMS encryption
